counterexample: u = aab, v = aba: the word baa is fixed by every rewrite, so its class {baa} is smaller than its counting class {aab, aba, baa}. All 33 relations of length 3-4 fail (EXP-C01-04).

history.new: The negative answer is implied by the Golod-Shafarevich/Anick lower bound H >= 1/(1 - qx + x^k) for one-relator algebras (Anick 1982; Piontkovski 1999) - a single relation cannot make the classes as coarse as counting classes. Historian audit, reviews/historian_C01_C02.md.

statement:
For every relation u <-> v over {a,b} with u != v and equal symbol counts, the generated congruence
coincides with counting (Parikh) equivalence on all words of length >= |u|.
title: H-C01-4: a single rearranging relation generates counting equivalence on long words (refuted)
